title: Detroit City Council Districts 2026
description:
Note: This council district layer goes into effect on January 1, 2026. The council district layer in effect until December 31st, 2025 can be found here

This Council Districts map is for illustrative purposes only and the City of Detroit makes no representations as to its accuracy. For the official geographic boundaries, please refer to the geographical boundaries formally approved by the Detroit City Council on February 6, 2024. For convenience, a link to the formally approved boundaries may be found here. The reapportioned City Council District boundaries take effect on January 1, 2026.

Following each census, Detroit City Council is required by the 2012 Detroit City Charter to redraw the boundaries of the City's seven non at-large districts to be "as nearly of equal population as practicable, contiguous, compact and in accordance with any other criteria permitted by law" (Sec. 3-108).City Council selected the boundaries illustrated here by an 8-1 vote on February 6, 2024. These boundaries will be used to determine resident districts when voting in 2025 municipal elections, and will officially take effect January 1, 2026.

title: Detroit Council District Kindergarten and Early Childhood Analysis
description:
Overview

This feature service provides council district level information for Detroit, combining education access and local representation details in a single layer. It supports analysis of kindergarten enrollment, early childhood program availability, and district administrative context.

Included Content
  • Council district boundaries with district identifiers, area, and representative information.
  • Kindergarten and early childhood measures including enrollment totals, counts of schools and programs, and indicators related to Early On, Great Start to Readiness Program, Head Start blend, and special education services.
  • District reference information such as associated ZIP codes, neighborhoods, website links, email contacts, and partner details.
  • Planning and analysis metrics that summarize supply, demand, gaps, and related program counts for district-level comparison.
Geographic Coverage

The service covers Detroit city council districts and is suitable for local-scale planning, outreach, and district comparison within the city.

Use Cases
  • Reviewing kindergarten access and early childhood program coverage by council district.
  • Supporting education planning, community outreach, and district-level reporting.
  • Connecting civic representation information with neighborhood and ZIP code context.
snippet: This layer summarizes Detroit council district boundaries with kindergarten enrollment, early childhood program counts, and representative contact information for district-level analysis.

title: IFFDetroitECEGap2024_CityCouncilDistricts2013
description: IFF provide D3 with this dataset, as well as this methodology. This layer is an output of an R script that uses (1) the ECE provider data from November 2024 and (2) 2024 ECE demand data (from 2024 ESRI single year age data and ACS 2019-2023) to calculate ECE service gaps and quality gaps. The gaps are calculated for ages 0-2, 3-5 and 0-5, and for state subsidized (CDC), federal subsidized (Head Start), and state subsidized Pre-K (GSRP) programs. Quality ECE providers are subset based on their GSQ quality levels of 3 and above and their slot capacity is defined as quality supply. Field names and descriptions are listed below, some longer field names have been truncated.
snippet: This layer contains the ECE service gaps and quality service gaps. It also contains the demand for ECE at the council district level.
